topic: The Additive Property of Normal Distributions: Gaussian + Gaussian = Gaussian

outline.topic: The Additive Property of Normal Distributions: Gaussian + Gaussian = Gaussian

sections.title: Introduction: The Intuition of Summing Noise
sections.content: Begin with a visual scenario: A robot arm is trying to reach a target. The jitter in the motor (X) is Normal, and the jitter in the sensor (Y) is also Normal. When we combine these errors (Z = X + Y), what does the resulting distribution look like? We introduce the concept that the sum of independent normal random variables remains normal.
sections.example: A delivery drone experiences random wind gusts (Distribution X) and random vibration noise from its battery (Distribution Y). We want to show how these two 'bells' merge into one.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Parameters of the Bell Curve
sections.content: Briefly recap that a Normal Distribution N(μ, σ²) is defined by mean (μ) and variance (σ²). Use a visual animation: shift the peak (μ) and change the width (σ²) to demonstrate how parameters change the shape.
sections.example: Visualizing a tall, skinny bell curve vs. a wide, flat one as 'High Precision' vs. 'High Uncertainty'.

sections.title: The Core Rule: Adding Means and Variances
sections.content: Present the mathematical theorem: If X ~ N(μ₁, σ₁²) and Y ~ N(μ₂, σ₂²), then X + Y ~ N(μ₁ + μ₂, σ₁² + σ₂²). Emphasize that means add linearly, and variances add directly (crucially, not standard deviations).
sections.example: A basketball player's shooting center (mean) shifts by the sum of their coach's bias (μ1) and their own nerves (μ2). The total 'wobble' (variance) is the sum of the physical air resistance variance and the player's inconsistent hand motion variance.

sections.title: Visual Proof: The 'Convolution' Concept
sections.content: Show an animation where two Gaussian density functions 'slide' past each other (the mathematical process of convolution). As they overlap and add, the resulting curve remains a perfect bell shape. Contrast this with adding non-normal distributions, which do not maintain the same shape.
sections.example: An animation showing two 2D Gaussian 'clouds' merging into one larger, centered 'cloud' as they are summed together.

sections.title: Application & Wrap-up
sections.content: Summarize why this is powerful: In real-world systems, we rarely track individual sources of error. By knowing this rule, we can treat the total system error as a single Normal distribution, greatly simplifying complex calculations.
sections.example: Final slide: A complex factory line with 10 different measurement stations. We don't calculate them one by one; we use the 'Sum of Gaussians' rule to predict the final output quality in one step.

storyboard.title: Introduction: The Intuition of Summing Noise
lecture_lines: Robot arms jitter due to motor and sensor errors.
We model these jitters as Normal distributions.
Combining these errors creates a new error distribution.
Surprisingly, this sum remains a Normal distribution.
Let's explore why this happens.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: Parameters of the Bell Curve
lecture_lines: Normal distributions are defined by mean and variance.
The mean shifts the bell curve's peak.
The variance controls the bell curve's width.

storyboard.title: The Core Rule: Adding Means and Variances
lecture_lines: If X and Y are Normal, their sum is Normal.
The new mean is the sum of means.
The new variance is the sum of variances.
Note: Variances add, not standard deviations.
This simple rule handles complex error accumulation.

storyboard.title: Visual Proof: The 'Convolution' Concept
lecture_lines: Convolution combines two functions into one.
Gaussians convolved together produce another Gaussian.
Adding Gaussian densities maintains the bell shape.
Non-normal shapes do not follow this rule.
The result is a broader, smoother curve.

storyboard.title: Application & Wrap-up
lecture_lines: In real systems, we sum many noise sources.
This rule simplifies complex error analysis.
We treat the total noise as one Gaussian.
